name: CivicLens
tagline: AI triage and analytics for citizen complaints
problem: Towns and campuses get thousands of complaints via apps, calls and social media
Clerks route them by hand, in English, Tamil and Tanglish
Duplicates pile up while a live wire waits behind a parking complaint
Hotspots and SLA breaches stay invisible until there is a crisis

stats.label: of Tamil Nadu's people live in urban areas (Census 2011, approx.)
complaints repeat an open issue (our synthetic stream; varies)

solution: Every new complaint is routed, prioritised and de-duplicated in ~3 ms
Safety rules plus an ML model set P1-P4 and say why
DBSCAN and Poisson tests flag hotspots and wards that are suddenly worse
Survival curves and a breach model warn before the SLA is missed

architecture: Browser UI -> vanilla JS, SVG/canvas charts, live queue and map
app.py -> stdlib ThreadingHTTPServer, JSON API, input validation
text + lexicon -> Tamil-safe tokens, graphemes, bilingual concepts
models -> NB, OvR logistic regression, urgency rules + model
dedup + hotspot -> MinHash LSH, haversine, DBSCAN, Poisson test
sla + topics -> Kaplan-Meier, breach LR, spherical k-means
algorithms: Multinomial Naive Bayes - department routing baseline
TF-IDF logistic regression (OvR, SGD) - routing + urgency
MinHash + LSH banding + haversine - duplicate incidents
DBSCAN (grid index) - spatial hotspots per department
Poisson z-test - emerging ward hotspots vs 4-week baseline
Kaplan-Meier + logistic regression - SLA curves and breach risk
Spherical k-means++ + silhouette - topics in Other
innovation: Tamil grapheme tokenizer + bilingual concepts: one model, three scripts
Duplicates matched across languages using text, place and time
Safety rules never wait for a model; the model never hides why
Every metric measured against planted ground truth

results.label: routing accuracy, 615 held-out (94.2% on unseen phrasing)

Tamil-only complainants are served as well as English ones
